why: I compared each check's PASS/FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 asks for more than its line does. Expect line 1 only says the tool prints `<file>:<line>: <error>` for every invalid row and exits 1 or 0. It never forbids other output. Yet Check 1 requires that clean.jsonl "prints nothing to stdout" and that bad.jsonl "prints exactly two lines", and it fails on "any other output lines". So a summary line or an "OK" message would fail a tool that meets the words. Check 1 also fails a tool that reports the whitespace-only line 4, but the brief's own Advisory says whitespace-only handling is "not pass/fail", so the two contradict each other. Check 4 also requires that the test run "passes". Line 4 only asks for tests to exist; passing belongs to line 6. These stricter conditions should be under Advisory, not in PASS or FAIL.
